To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hateful users can be identified by analyzing their network structure and that this approach outperforms content based approaches for the detection and characterization of hateful users.

(i) hateful users differ from non hateful ones in terms of activity patterns, word choice, and network structure; (ii) hateful and non hateful users are densely and sparsely connected, respectively; (iii) hateful users are also more likely to be suspended by Twitter; (iv) hateful users are densely clustered in the retweet graph; (v) hateful and suspended users can be detected using semi-supervised learning on the retweet graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and detection of hateful users on Twitter.
the characterization and detection of hateful users on Twitter, by leveraging the information contained in the network of connections.

the following contributions: (a) we present an approach to collect and annotate users on Twitter that is robust to the incompletness and noisiness issues of OSN text; (b) we characterize hateful users by comparing them to normal users and suspended users; (c) we formulate the problem of detecting hateful users as a graph semi-supervised learning problem and show that it outperforms content based approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hateful users can be identified by analyzing their network structure, without relying on the content they post.
our work is the first to characterize hateful users on Twitter, and to show that hateful users are more densely connected than normal users.
our approach is able to detect hateful users on Twitter with high accuracy and that hateful users differ in terms of their network structure, activity and content from normal ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel methodology to detect hateful users in Twitter.

we present a novel methodology for the collection and annotation of hateful users on Twitter, and we characterize and detect hateful users by exploiting their activity patterns, their word usage and their network structure.

1) hateful users can be characterized using a combination of their activity patterns and word usage, and that they differ from normal users and from users that were suspended from the platform, 2) hateful users are densely interconnected and this can be leveraged to detect hateful users with high accuracy, and 3) the detection of hateful users is more effective than the detection of suspended users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hateful users are different from other users and this difference can be exploited to detect hateful users.
hateful users differ significantly from normal users and that their behavior can be exploited to characterize and detect hateful users on Twitter.
hateful users are different from normal ones in their activity patterns, their content and in their network structure.
